content.study:
Article 373 (“Power of President to make order in respect of persons under preventive detention in certain cases”) of the Constitution of India has been omitted by constitutional amendment.

Status: Repealed / Omitted.
It is not current working law in the territory of India.

Examination Instruction:
When answering university or judicial service questions, note that Article 373 is omitted and identify the living constitutional or statutory provision that currently governs the subject matter.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the constitutional status and historical context of Article 373 (Power of President to make order in respect of persons under preventive detention in certain cases).
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
I. INTRODUCTION & STATUS
Article 373 of the Constitution of India (“Power of President to make order in respect of persons under preventive detention in certain cases”) is omitted. It does not form part of the living, enforceable constitutional text.

II. HISTORICAL BACKGROUND
The provision was repealed/omitted by constitutional amendment to remove obsolete structures, harmonize constitutional governance, or eliminate transitional provisions.

III. CURRENT GOVERNING HEADING
Examinees must identify the living provision that now regulates this field (e.g. general powers of Parliament, corresponding statutory enactments, or alternative constitutional mechanisms).

IV. CONCLUSION
Cite Article 373 strictly as a repealed/omitted heading. Do not apply its text to contemporary 2026 dispute scenarios.
